title: Pre-registration Adoption Gaps
bottleneck: Pre-registration of hypotheses and analysis plans would curb p-hacking and HARKing, but adoption outside clinical trials and parts of psychology is minimal. Researchers resist the perceived loss of flexibility, and journals rarely require it. Without it, readers cannot distinguish confirmatory tests from exploratory fishing expeditions.
why_it_blocks: Without pre-registration, the line between confirmatory and exploratory findings stays blurred, inflating false-discovery rates. The credibility of entire fields rests on a distinction most papers do not make. Journals that mandate pre-registration see cleaner literatures, but they remain the exception.
current_state: Registered Reports are growing slowly; most fields have no pre-registration norm at all. Mandates from journals have driven adoption where tried, suggesting top-down requirements work. Pre-registration is a low-cost reform with demonstrated benefits where adopted.

sources.title: Evidence and the Design and Reform of Scientific Institutions (Nintil)
